result.title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
result.summary: Neural decoding of visual experience from electroencephalography (EEG) has achieved strong performance in intra-subject settings, but current methods fail to generalize across individuals: on the standard 200-way benchmark THINGS-EEG-2, top-1 accuracy drops from above 80% within subjects to about 32% for an unseen subject. Adapting a pre-trained encoder to new subjects and sessions typically requires labeled data, a bottleneck whose collection time severely limits practical device deployment. In a practical Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), however, the possible outcomes are known in advance and form a gallery of candidates, and the unlabeled EEG of the user accumulates as soon as the device is used. We propose a new setting, incremental transductive calibration, in which the decoder is calibrated regularly on all the unlabeled EEG received so far and on the known gallery, without any labels. This setting is closer to the conditions of a deployed BCI than the zero-shot and batch evaluations in current use. We evaluate it with a protocol in which queries arrive one at a time, with unknown and possibly unequal frequencies, and each query is decoded before it is used for calibration. In this setting, we introduce GALA : GAllery-Level Alignment, a label-free calibration method which registers the unlabeled EEG embeddings onto the gallery through shrinkage whitening, hubness correction and a Sinkhorn--Procrustes alignment with query frequencies estimated from the buffer, updated after every query. On THINGS-EEG-2, with a gallery of 200 images, it raises the top-1 accuracy on a new subject from 28% to 67% over 53 minutes of use. Across 60 evaluation settings that vary the gallery size, the query frequencies and the number of repetitions averaged per query, GALA is the most accurate label-free method in every setting, 6.6 points above the best competing method on average at the end of the stream.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向 EEG 视觉解码的跨被试泛化，提出「增量直推式校准」设定：候选图库已知、用户 EEG 无标签累积，并用收缩白化、hubness 校正与 Sinkhorn–Procrustes 对齐将嵌入注册到图库，实现逐查询的无标签在线校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其无标签在线校准与嵌入几何对齐手段（白化、hubness 校正、Sinkhorn–Procrustes）可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 表示的持续对齐与候选筛选问题，但 EEG 解码本身不涉及推理状态生成，联系较远。
